maya: Quick triage: we need to finalize the dedicated capacity policy for the Q3 commercial release. Topics: reserved pool guarantees, burst lane behavior, billing for burst, carryover asks, and autoscale cooldown. Can we decide today?
omar: I'll run the policy thread. TL;DR proposal incoming: guaranteed baseline (no eviction), soft-burst lane (preemptible) governed by a token-bucket + per-tenant ceiling, burst billed separately.
lucy: Runtime constraints: soft-burst must allow in-flight session completion. We can preempt new requests but should drain existing KV cache sessions. Also prefer a short autoscale cooldown (30s) to avoid flapping.
ben: SRE note: unbounded burst causes p99 blowups in our simulator. We recommend enforced caps. Doing token-buckets per tenant looks best operationally.
ben: sim snippet we used: {"burst_capacity": 300, "refill_per_min": 30, "max_burst_minutes": 20} — gave acceptable p99 under mixed load.
alia: Sales/Customer ask: a few enterprise pilots want unused reserved capacity rolled forward (carryover) up to 10% for 1 billing cycle. They also want a simple SLA statement showing burst is not guaranteed.
docs: FYI — billing language will need a short clause and an FAQ. If burst is metered we should show estimated worst-case bill for a 2x burst scenario.
omar: Concrete policy proposal: 1) Reserved baseline = guaranteed. 2) Soft-burst = per-tenant token bucket, preemptible; when exhausted, new requests are rejected with clear error code. 3) Billing = baseline billed as committed reservation; burst metered per-second (rounded up to minute for invoice), with a hard monthly cap configurable per customer. 4) Carryover = offered as a paid add-on pilot: roll up to 10% unused to next month, expires after 30 days.
maya: Launch readiness checklist: - Policy locked + product doc - Engineering feature flag in place - Billing and legal clause drafted - 3 pilot customers signed for canary - Observability (burst labels and p99 dashboards)
lucy: Implementation items: routing: baseline lane -> guaranteed pool; burst lane -> opportunistic nodes; admission controller enforces token bucket and per-tenant cap; session drain hooks for preemption; metric labels tenant_id/commitment/burst_used; feature-flag gate.
ben: I'll run expanded sims for multi-tenant storms and a sustained 15-minute spike. Will post results.
sre-bot: sim queued id=6202, config="burst_capacity=300, refill=30/m, max_burst=20m", eta=2026-06-04T18:00:00Z
omar: Decision asks: 1) Is per-second metering OK (more accurate) vs per-minute (simpler)? 2) Do we want immediate rejection or queue-with-timeout when burst is exhausted?
alia: Customers prefer predictable billing (per-minute OK) but also want the ability to cap spend. So we should support a hard spend cap per account. Queueing is risky for user-facing latency-sensitive flows. They prefer fast fail with actionable error.
lucy: Engineering prefers immediate rejection + helpful error with retry-after and suggested fallback model. Queueing introduces complexity and latency tail risk.
ben: Agreed with Lucy. Fast fail is operationally simpler and safer.
omar: OK settled: metering per-second on backend, invoice rounding per-minute; behavior = immediate rejection with error code 429b (burst_exhausted) and Retry-After header. Offer carryover as paid add-on with 10% cap.
maya: Can we set rollout targets? Lucy - feature-flag PR by 2026-06-01. Canary with 3 pilots by 2026-06-10. GA if canary meets: p95 latency regression <8%, error escalations <3 in 30d, billing docs published.
lucy: ETA: feature flag + admission-controller changes by 2026-06-01. Need two-week canary window.
ben: sims will be complete by 2026-06-03, I'll attach results to the thread.
docs: I'll draft the customer FAQ and billing clause; will sync with Maya and Legal after policy lock.
maya: Alright, last call for objections to token-bucket + immediate-reject approach?
omar: no objections from product.
ben: SRE aligned, pending sim results to pick capacity numbers.
lucy: Engineering aligned. Will add KV cache tags to avoid memory retention during preemptions.
alia: Sales aligned, will surface pilot customers and their billing constraints by EOD.
maya: I'll schedule a lock call tomorrow 9:30am PT to sign off and publish the pilot terms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
